sasha: Heads up, deploy-bot just proposed a minor bump for the logging change in #PR-3489. It only tweaks error messages and a panic -> error return, no API change. I'm pretty sure this should be a patch.

release-bot: deploy analysis: touched files: src/logger/*, src/checkout/error_handling.rs, docs/observability.md -> heuristics: src change + non-doc -> candidate minor. Tagging rule: src changes default to minor unless PR title includes [PATCH] or override flag.

kevin: That heuristic is too broad. Small internal refactors or error-handling hardening shouldn't force a minor semver move. Patch and note in changelog.

sasha: Agreed. We try to keep minors reserved for user-visible features or breaking changes.

tori: Quick workaround: retitle PR to include [PATCH] or run `tools/releasebot release --patch-only` from CI. We should also document this pattern in the release playbook.

kevin: Long term: can we teach deploy-bot to inspect API surface? e.g., changes in public headers, exported structs, or route signatures => minor, else patch. Also consider a whitelist: changes to /docs, /tests, /ci, and error-handling files => patch.

release-bot: noted: feature-request filed -> rfc/semver-heuristics #12 (automated-surface-diff). Manual override accepted: `--force-patch` or PR title tokens: [PATCH], [MINOR], [FORCE].

sasha: I'll retitle and kick off the override job. Posting change note: "v2.5.1 (patch) - clarify logger stack traces; no behavioral change" :thumbsup:

kevin: one more ask: can release-bot annotate the PR explaining why it picked minor so we can triage quickly? Often people just see a tag and panic. A one-line justification would help.

release-bot: enhancement noted. Will add a rationale header to automatic tagging: "reason: src files touched -> default minor".

tori: Filing a tiny follow-up RFC to add a 'surface-sensitive' mode and to add a fallback preference for patch during stable windows. Link: https://git.internal/rex/rfcs/13-semver-heuristics

sasha: Thanks — this saved us a noisy minor. Closing thread.
